blocks.text: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — Cebu’s market continues to grow, with around five million people to feed. However, local agricultural production remains insufficient to meet the province’s food requirements, according to Rey Calooy, chairman of the Philippine Inno-Ventures Agriculture Cooperative (PIVAC). As a result, Cebu has to source food supplies from abroad and neighboring provinces to meet local demand. READ: Central Visayas pushes food security drive as inflation, poverty concerns persist Calooy said achieving food sustainability in Cebu would require government support and technological advancements in the agricultural sector.
